access_policy: research_a/research_b are already-used research data; confirmation, locked and legacy final ranges stay closed this round.

budget.retry_policy: At most one same-configuration, same-seed technical retry per incomplete fit; a completed fit is never rerun because of its score.
budget.round_scope: The 9000-second cap covers preparation, six fits, inference and both analyses; CUDA fits run one at a time.

research_a.measurement: Synchronized CUDA; same full input keys; warmup excluded; shared preprocessing reported separately

research_b.measurement: Synchronized CUDA; same full input keys; warmup excluded; shared preprocessing reported separately

calibration.basis: Six archived 10-day baseline fits on research_a/research_b, re-scored from their frozen predictions and evaluation targets; frozen before any 40-day fit.

hypothesis: Standardizing the official label within each full training timestamp, then restoring the centered training-pool variance with one constant, makes the target scale comparable across market states and improves out-of-sample ranking against the raw-label 10-day reference under the unchanged gates. Passing that comparison would not by itself show the new standardization beats the centered control.

label_transform.assumption_status: minimal unverified assumption for this project; the public cross-sectional z-score precedent does not establish that variance matching improves this model or beats the centered control
label_transform.cross_section: one complete timestamp of the frozen 10-day training pool, all stocks and all eight sample times; never a random mini-batch
label_transform.evaluation: official raw labels for every ranking, long-short, turnover and raw-label error; centered-label error and the optimized transformed-target loss are named separately
label_transform.fallback: timestamp-centered training-label mean over the selected rows, identical to the centered control; not re-estimated from y*
label_transform.formula: r = float64(float32(y)); z = r - mean_t(r); q = z / std_t(r) if std_t(r) > 0 else 0; c = std(z) / std(q); y* = float32(c q)
label_transform.inference: network(x) * target_scale; c is never multiplied back and no future timestamp mean or standard deviation is added

research_a.c_formula: std(centered training labels, ddof=0) / std(q, ddof=0) over the complete training pool
research_a.fallback_basis: timestamp-centered training-label mean in the same float32 representation used by the centered control; never re-estimated from the transformed targets
research_a.formula: q = (r - mean_t(r)) / std_t(r); y* = c q with c = std(z) / std(q), all ddof=0
research_a.scope: every row of each full training timestamp in the selected training pool; computed once before mini-batches and before the min-history mask

research_b.c_formula: std(centered training labels, ddof=0) / std(q, ddof=0) over the complete training pool
research_b.fallback_basis: timestamp-centered training-label mean in the same float32 representation used by the centered control; never re-estimated from the transformed targets
research_b.formula: q = (r - mean_t(r)) / std_t(r); y* = c q with c = std(z) / std(q), all ddof=0
research_b.scope: every row of each full training timestamp in the selected training pool; computed once before mini-batches and before the min-history mask

label_transform.pool_constant: c is computed once from every selected training row before mini-batches and before the min-history mask

public_precedent.use: Qlib applies CSZScoreNorm per datetime; this round only borrows that public cross-sectional z-score template. Matching the centered pool variance with one constant c is this project's control design, not a copied Qlib configuration.

label_transform.target_scale: raw official training-label standard deviation, unchanged from the reference
label_transform.zero_variance: zero-variance timestamps keep all rows with q=0; the whole-pool std(q)=0 case fails before training

basis.rss_formula: round_up_256(1.25 x measured peak host RSS)
basis.wall_formula: round_up_300(1.25 x (measured preprocessing + 1500 x measured seconds/step) + 300s save/check slack)

notes: Six mandatory CSZ fits. The six raw-label and six centered arms are reused, never refitted. No other label transform, standardization strength, step count, seed or loss is searched.
only_factor: training target raw official return -> float32(c q), where q is the full-timestamp z-score and c = std(centered labels)/std(q), both ddof=0 over the complete training pool; target_scale stays the raw-label std; network, inputs, steps, batch order, MSE, seeds and dates fixed

policy.exposure_policy: Steps, batch size, learning rate and recipe stay fixed for this round; a larger pool gets no extra steps because that would confound coverage with compute.
policy.interpretation_rule: A non-accept result bounds what equal-compute date expansion achieves; it does not establish that more history is uninformative.
policy.primary_metric: paired daily all-eight-time RankIC, seed-mean per day before pairing

statistics.sensitivity_rule: Report both block lengths; conflicting conclusions are inconclusive, and neither is chosen after seeing results.

progress.rule: Seed 11 is printed and archived only as progress after all six fits; no decision is made until all three seeds and both windows are complete.

recipe_fixed.target_std_fit: raw official selected training labels, full 10-day pool

reference_source.note: The six raw-label fits and the six centered fits are reused, never refitted. Their weights, predictions, training keys, labels and configs are checked before the freeze.

source_delta.note: Only adapter.py and config.py differ from the centered snapshot. The centered transform block is byte-identical; the CSZ method is the new branch.

statistics.sensitivity_rule: Report both block lengths; conflicting conclusions are inconclusive, and neither is chosen after seeing results.

config.hypothesis: Centering training labels within each full timestamp, while keeping the raw-label target standard deviation, reduces unlearnable market-level noise and improves out-of-sample ranking enough to clear the retained raw-label 10-day reference under the unchanged gates.

Cross-sectional timestamp z-scores rescaled by one training-pool constant to the centered labels' variance reduce cross-regime target-scale instability and improve out-of-sample ranking against the raw-label 10-day reference under the unchanged gates.
40 training dates improve subsequent ranking and long-short stability

exposure.interpretation: All three arms use 1500 x 32 = 48,000 sample exposures on the same training dates and seeds; only the training target differs.
